title: First gate runs on dfmodel against the pre-fix product, on two machines
hypothesis: Running the whole gate, holdout included, against the product before the follow-through fix shows which cases discriminate on qoder/dfmodel, whether the fix carries over to a restated case, and whether the keep cases are stable enough to catch regressions.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel only for the counted samples, frozen baseline 22806d9^ (product 0.1.27, fork 1.4.0-rotom.2) against candidate 0.2.4 (fork 1.5.2-rotom.1; commits 8f74604, 919ad0d and c8737e9 carry the same product code). mac1 (macOS 27.3) one full gate --holdout; mac3 (macOS 27.0) one full gate --holdout plus five more pairs of each continuation case and eight pairs of the mixed case. One mac3 mixed run used gpt-6.1-sol under the old manifest and is not counted. Failures were read from recorded checks and tool calls without model calls.
result: Climb behavior-authorized-follow-through: baseline 7/11, candidate 11/11. Holdout variant: baseline 3/11, candidate 10/11, the restated case discriminates more than the original. Keep: export-symptom and scoped-read 2/2 on both arms; status-is-not-authorization baseline 11/11, candidate 10/11 (one run executed the pipeline after a status question despite an explicit no-execution turn); mixed-decision-ownership baseline 9/11, candidate 6/11, split between re-running completed scripts on both arms and fenced or annotated JSON replies on the candidate only. The continuation suite did not state the raw-JSON reply rule the fixture suites state; it now does for JSON-schema cases, which voids the mixed samples. Attribution limit: the arms differ by much more than the follow-through rule, so none of this attributes a difference to one change; same-product on/off arms are needed for that.

title: Remove behavior-mixed-decision-ownership from the gate: its baseline is not stable on dfmodel
hypothesis: With the raw-JSON reply rule stated, the mixed case's remaining failures on qoder/dfmodel would disappear and it could stay a keep case; if the frozen baseline still fails, it cannot tell a regression from the model's own habit and leaves the keep set, as decided before the recalibration run.
measurement: qoder/dfmodel, mac3, frozen 22806d9^ (product 0.1.27) against candidate main 5572363 (0.2.4 with the bb8ddba6 fork rebuild), five pairs.
result: Baseline 4/5, candidate 4/5. Both failures are the same: after migrate.mjs the model ran apply-internal.mjs a second time as a check, so runs.log had three lines and secondPhaseActionsBound and internalChoiceNotRepeated were false. All ten replies were raw JSON. Re-running a logging command to verify happened on both arms in every dfmodel round (11 pairs earlier: baseline 2, candidate 3), so it is the model's habit rather than a product difference, and a keep case whose baseline fails cannot flag a regression. Removed from loop/gate.json; the case and its oracle remain in the continuation suite. Whether verifying by re-running a side-effecting command is wrong is left open: it would need its own case with a judge that says so explicitly.
